steps: Confirm alarm features absent (weight loss, bleeding, anaemia, nocturnal symptoms, onset >50) and basic tests normal.
Diet/lifestyle: regular meals, fibre adjustment, trial of low-FODMAP with dietitian; address triggers.
Symptom-targeted drugs: antispasmodics for pain, laxatives for IBS-C, loperamide for IBS-D.
Low-dose tricyclic or SSRI for pain/global symptoms; psychological therapies (CBT/gut-directed hypnotherapy).
Reassurance and a positive diagnosis; review and safety-net.

confirm: Chronic abdominal pain related to defecation with altered bowel habit and no alarm features; positive symptom-based (Rome IV) diagnosis after excluding organic disease.

investigations.test: FBC, CRP, coeliac serology, faecal calprotectin
